message.content: {"candidates":[{"sequence":"EQYTSNGTLE","hypothesis":"10-aa polar-anchor hypothesis: Tyr/Leu provide limited V66 packing; Thr/Ser target T64 without requiring buried N65. Removes bulky Trp from poorly discriminating round-one motifs.","expected_discrimination":"Test higher compatibility across MSA, where T64/V66 are more exposed, than BOTH controls; SASA layer-count differences make this provisional."},{"sequence":"KDTYSPGTLEK","hypothesis":"11-aa shape hypothesis: SPG biases a bend, with Tyr/Leu bracketing a small polar surface near T64/V66/G67.","expected_discrimination":"Test adaptation to MSA V66–G68 spacing of 5.5 Å versus 5.2 Å in 8A9L and 5.9 Å in 6CU7; differences are small."},{"sequence":"EKSFTPGTQLEK","hypothesis":"12-aa shape/polar hypothesis: retain TPG but replace Trp with Phe and limit hydrophobic density. Round-one TPG-containing peptides did not achieve positive contrast.","expected_discrimination":"Seek a constrained T64/V66-facing pose across MSA rather than the broader control contacts observed previously; weaker binding to each control must be verified."},{"sequence":"DQYTNAGTQVEK","hypothesis":"12-aa flexible polar-anchor hypothesis: NAG replaces a proline turn, permitting accommodation of all three MSA geometries without demanding N65 side-chain access.","expected_discrimination":"Test recognition of exposed T64/V66 plus moderately accessible G67; 6CU7 is less accessible, while discrimination from 8A9L must arise from pose geometry."},{"sequence":"EKQYSPATQLEKD","hypothesis":"13-aa shape hypothesis: SPA reduces glycine flexibility relative to SPG; separated Tyr/Leu anchors avoid an extended hydrophobic run.","expected_discrimination":"Test the MSA V63–V70 span of 7.7–8.1 Å against 8.6 Å in 8A9L and 8.3 Å in 6CU7, without assuming direct V63 binding."},{"sequence":"KETYQSGTQLSEK","hypothesis":"13-aa polar-anchor hypothesis: Ser/Thr/Gln support T64 recognition, with Tyr/Leu as modest V66 anchors and balanced charged termini.","expected_discrimination":"Prioritize T64/V66 over N65, whose SASA varies strongly among MSA conformers; require lower predicted compatibility with both controls despite similar local backbone geometry."},{"sequence":"DEQYTPGTLQSTEK","hypothesis":"14-aa acidic-solubility hypothesis: retain YTPG from round-one EEQYTPGNFQSTEE but replace Phe with Leu and reduce reliance on Asn anchoring. Parent minimum-MSA contact density was 0.143 versus maximum-control 3.5.","expected_discrimination":"Test whether reduced aromatic surface reverses control-biased contacts while maintaining T64/V66 anchoring; acidic residues are solvent-facing, not proposed patch salt bridges."},{"sequence":"KEQFTPGTSQLEKD","hypothesis":"14-aa balanced-charge shape hypothesis: Phe/Leu flank a TPGTS bend, while terminal Lys/Glu/Asp improve solubility without assigning unsupported electrostatic contacts.","expected_discrimination":"Seek MSA-compatible V66–G68 geometry at 5.5 Å and penalize both the shorter 8A9L and longer 6CU7 spacing; prediction is speculative."},{"sequence":"EQHSTPGTQLSNKE","hypothesis":"14-aa low-aromatic alternative: His/Leu replace the Trp/Phe pair, reducing nonspecific hydrophobic capture while preserving a polar turn.","expected_discrimination":"Test whether T64-directed polar contacts survive in all MSA structures while control contact density falls; His introduces an experimentally testable pH dependence."},{"sequence":"EKQYTSAPTQLSQDEK","hypothesis":"16-aa shape hypothesis: SAP provides a less flexible bend than glycine-rich motifs, with only two separated hydrophobic anchors.","expected_discrimination":"Test a compact pose around T64/V66/G67 that fits all MSA structures but not BOTH controls; avoid dependence on the more buried G68/A69."},{"sequence":"KDEQYTSNGTQLSTQEK","hypothesis":"17-aa polar-scaffold hypothesis: extend a small Tyr/Leu recognition core with soluble polar flanks rather than adding aromatic anchors. Round-one longer scaffolds still favored controls.","expected_discrimination":"Evaluate whether flanks remain solvent-exposed while the core recognizes MSA T64/V66 accessibility; reject poses gaining contacts through exposed control V70."},{"sequence":"EQKSTLQPGTYSNQTEK","hypothesis":"16-aa reversed-anchor hypothesis: reverse Leu/Tyr order around QPGT to sample a different binding orientation from round-one aromatic motifs.","expected_discrimination":"Test simultaneous accommodation of the MSA T64–V66 distance of 6.7–6.9 Å and V66–G68 distance of 5.5 Å; both controls must score worse."},{"sequence":"DEKSYTQAPGTQLSNQTEK","hypothesis":"18-aa shape/charge hypothesis: APG introduces a localized bend; acidic/polar flanks discourage broad hydrophobic surface association.","expected_discrimination":"Seek a geometry-selective T64/V66 pose rather than generic exposed-patch binding, particularly to 8A9L; 6CU7 discrimination may additionally reflect lower accessibility."},{"sequence":"KEQSTYQNGTQLSNTQSEKDE","hypothesis":"20-aa flexible-scaffold alternative: retain polar-rich chemistry but use Tyr/Leu instead of Trp/Phe and omit proline to test whether imposed turns caused MSA incompatibility.","expected_discrimination":"All round-one contrasts were negative; test improved minimum-MSA versus maximum-control contact density while requiring compatibility with each MSA and reduced compatibility with each control."},{"sequence":"DEKQSTYQAPGTQLSNTQSEKDEK","hypothesis":"23-aa extended shape hypothesis: a compact YQAPGTQL core supplies restrained hydrophobic anchoring; balanced, polar flanks probe soluble presentation. All candidates are cysteine-free linear peptides.","expected_discrimination":"Test whether a localized core exploits MSA V66–G68 geometry and T64 exposure without recruiting control V63/V70 surfaces; longer flanks must not create nonspecific control contacts."}]}
